text:
maria: heads up — noticed steady KV cache memory growth on the on-prem cluster (private) when running long chat sessions (20k+ tokens). growth isn't linear but creeps up over hours, and OOMs only on machines with constrained host-memory.

aj: any recent config changes on the private deploys? MTU, cgroup limits, jemalloc tunables?

maria: we rolled a small kernel update last week + bumped `vm.max_map_count` for a different perf test. nothing else intentional. attaching quick samples:
```
Private host (after 12h): rss=120G, kv_resident=85G, page_faults (minor)=1.2M
Dedicated (same workload): rss=96G, kv_resident=62G, minor pf=120k
Hosted (prod snapshots): rss=88G, kv_resident=58G, minor pf=105k
```

devin: those minor pf counts are a red flag. looks like repeated page-walking on the private hosts. could be fragmentation or different allocation paths (jemalloc vs system alloc). any difference in kernel version / hugepage usage?

maria: private is on custom onprem A100 nodes, kernel 5.15 + some vendor patches, hugepages disabled (we left it that way for other infra reasons). dedicated is GCP A100 with 5.19 stock. hosted uses our managed nodes with 6.x.

aj: also check NIC MTU — VPCs sometimes mask cross-host shared memory patterns when MTU mismatches force smaller batching windows. small MTU + cgroup cpu throttling can change scheduling and cause more KV slot churn.

liam: interesting — could kernel-level I/O or scheduling changes be causing different kernel selection in our runtime? if the optimized attention kernels fall back to safer slow paths we keep more KV state around longer which may increase resident memory.

maria: yes — observed that private nodes frequently hit scalar-fallback kernels for causally large sequences due to an AVX guard we added. fallback -> slower token throughput -> longer per-request lifetime -> more KV frames pinned.

perf-bot: automated trace uploaded: https://perf.internal/trace/2890123456 (summary: host-private: avg latency +24%, token throughput -18%, kv_residency +37%)

aj: can you repro with kernel 6.x in a private canary or enable hugepages as a quick test? would also like `jeprof` dumps and `pagemap` samples from the private host.

maria: repro steps attached inline:
```
# run long-ctx gen loop (replicate chat shards)
for i in $(seq 1 200); do 
  ./run_inference --model xlarge --seq 20k --batch 4 || break
done
# capture jemalloc stats
echo "arena.0.pactive: $(cat /proc/$(pgrep runner)/status 2>/dev/null)"
# gather pagemap sample (30s)
python scripts/pagemap-sample.py --pid $(pgrep runner) --out /tmp/pm.json
```

liam: also try toggling our batching heuristic: reduce max batching window to 12ms and enable early-evict for inactive slots. that should reduce KV pin time at cost of some throughput. run both variants on dedicated/hosted/private and compare kv_resident.

maria: ran quick experiment: on private, decreasing batch window -> kv_resident drops ~18% but latency tail increases 5-10ms p95. on dedicated same change yields 7% kv drop and negligible p95 change. hosted baseline already tuned so has <5% variance.

devin: that delta smells like environment coupling. private has fewer concurrent small requests, so our batching thresholds keep older KV frames alive waiting for coalescing. combined with fallback kernels increases lifetime.

aj: plan: 1) collect jemalloc + pagemap from private (maria) 2) run kernel 6.x canary on subset (devin/infra) 3) run microbench comparing batching-window and early-evict across all three deploys (liam) 4) add short-term guard: enforce early-evict on private for heavy longctx experiments.

maria: starting collection now, will drop artifacts in /artifacts/2890123456 and ping when done. tagging @devin for canary ticket.

liam: question — should we pursue a runtime change to prefer smaller kernels (more memory-friendly) when we detect on-prem constraints? i.e., kernel-selection policy that considers host memory pressure + MTU + kernel version.

aj: probably yes but prefer a short-term config toggle first. longer term a policy makes sense but we need telemetry to avoid oscillation. add telemetry: `kv.pin_time`, `kernel.fallback_count`, `batch.window_ms`, `minor_page_faults` per host.

maria: agreed. uploading first dumps now. will paste jemalloc snippets in thread when processed. thanks all :thumbsup:
